title: Police Are Using More Computer Tools to Watch Cities
summary:
Hundreds of police departments in the U.S. have real-time crime centers. These are places where officers can see information from many sources at once. Many now use artificial intelligence, or AI, software. One tool is called Fusus. It is made by a company named Axon.

Fusus brings together videos and information from police body cameras, police car cameras, 911 calls and other cameras. In 2024, just over 100 police agencies used it. Axon says that number has more than doubled since then.

Police say the tool saves time and helps them solve crimes. But some experts are worried. They say it is becoming very easy to watch lots of people, and innocent people could be swept up by mistake.

Axon's leader, Rick Smith, said the company values privacy. Courts have not yet decided where the limits should be. One law professor said lawmakers could make rules, such as limiting how long information is kept.
why_it_matters: Cameras are in many places people go every day, so rules about how they are used affect everyone's privacy.
